title: Figurative Language Practice 2
description: 4 short texts - 8 focused figurative language questions
subject: rla
passage:
TEXT A - Practice Hall

The drummer's mistake rippled through the group, and three players entered a measure too early.

TEXT B - Winter Street

The wind bit through the thin gloves.

TEXT C - Deadline

The final week collapsed into a blur of revisions, meetings, and late dinners.

TEXT D - Quiet Library

The old radiator coughed twice and then settled into a steady hum.

questions.explanation: Rippled transfers the spreading motion of water to an error moving through the group.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: The mistake caused the group to restart the entire piece from the beginning.
options.whyWrong: The passage describes several early entrances, not a full restart.

options.text: The mistake changed only the drummer’s part while the rest of the group continued normally.
options.whyWrong: The sentence says three other players entered early, so the effect spread beyond the drummer.

options.text: The mistake spread from one player to others.
The mistake made each player gradually play more quietly.
options.whyWrong: “Rippled” refers to the mistake spreading through the group, not to volume changing.

questions.prompt: What effect does the image emphasize?
questions.explanation: The ripple image highlights spreading consequences.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: how one small mistake affected several people
how long the mistake remained audible after the drummer corrected it
options.whyWrong: The image emphasizes spread from one player to others, not duration.

options.text: how difficult it was for the players to hear the drummer in the room
options.whyWrong: Nothing in the sentence suggests an acoustics problem.

options.text: how the mistake changed the type of rhythm the group was performing
options.whyWrong: The stated result is mistimed entrances, not a change in the composition’s rhythm type.

questions.explanation: Bit personifies the cold as something sharp and painful.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: The wind seemed intentionally hostile, as though it wanted to injure the person.
options.whyWrong: “Bit” intensifies the sensation of cold; it does not require the reader to assign intention to the wind.

options.text: The gloves tore because the wind was strong enough to damage them.
options.whyWrong: The sentence describes how the cold felt through thin gloves, not physical tearing.

options.text: The cold disappeared after briefly passing through the gloves.
options.whyWrong: “Bit” emphasizes sharp discomfort, not relief or disappearance.

options.text: The cold felt sharply painful.

questions.prompt: Why use bit instead of passed?
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: To identify the exact direction from which the wind was blowing.
options.whyWrong: The verb adds intensity to the sensation, not directional information.

options.text: To intensify the physical discomfort.
To make the description more formal and scientifically precise.
options.whyWrong: “Bit” is vivid figurative language, not technical wording.

options.text: To show that the gloves were unusually new and therefore ineffective.
options.whyWrong: The sentence only says the gloves are thin.

questions.explanation: The phrase compresses a hectic sequence into one indistinct period.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: The week ended suddenly because several scheduled activities were cancelled.
options.whyWrong: The sentence says the activities crowd together, not that they were cancelled.

options.text: Many events seemed compressed together.
The writer could no longer distinguish the days clearly because many events blended together.
options.whyWrong: The “blur” supports this idea, but “collapsed into” most directly suggests events compressing together rather than only a memory problem.

options.text: The project failed because the schedule physically broke down.
options.whyWrong: The phrase is figurative and describes how crowded the week felt, not a literal collapse or project failure.

questions.prompt: What effect does the phrase create?
questions.explanation: The figurative compression helps convey stress and rapid activity.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: It shows that the writer had carefully separated each task into an exact schedule.
options.whyWrong: The image does the opposite: it conveys tasks and days blending together.

options.text: It makes the week seem calm because the separate events no longer stand out.
options.whyWrong: The cluster of revisions, meetings, and late dinners creates pressure rather than calm.

options.text: It conveys how rushed and crowded the week felt.
It suggests the writer found the project easy once the final week began.
options.whyWrong: The crowded “blur” suggests strain and speed, not ease.

questions.explanation: The personification compares the rough sound to a cough.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: A person in the library briefly became ill near the radiator.
options.whyWrong: The subject is the radiator; “coughed” gives a human quality to its rough sound.

options.text: The radiator stopped working completely after making two noises.
options.whyWrong: It settles into a steady hum, so it continues operating.

options.text: The radiator produced a smooth, quiet sound from the moment it started.
options.whyWrong: The sentence contrasts two rough sounds with the steadier hum that follows.

options.text: A brief rough mechanical sound.

questions.explanation: The human sound makes the machine's rough start easy to imagine.
questions.rule: Use the exact wording and surrounding context as evidence.

options.text: a vivid sense of the radiator's imperfect start
a precise indication of how many years the radiator has been in the building
options.whyWrong: The image may make the radiator feel old or imperfect, but it gives no exact age.

options.text: a sense that the whole library is noisy and crowded
options.whyWrong: The image focuses on one brief mechanical sound in an otherwise quiet setting.

options.text: a medical explanation for why old heating systems can affect breathing
options.whyWrong: The language is figurative and describes a mechanical sound, not health effects.

curriculum.learningObjective: Apply figurative language reasoning across varied original short texts and explain answers from textual evidence.
